Anyone who can register or rename to a matching username gets linked to that local account without entering its password. Only use this if your provider controls usernames, and turn it off after migrating.
pages.settings.oidcGroupsHelp: Choose what happens when an OIDC user matches no configured group. The default is deny sign-in.

pages.metrics.partialWarning: Some metrics sources are unavailable: {sources}. Showing partial data.
pages.metrics.bouncersDescription: Remediation-component calls grouped by name, with the decision API mode and the routes that generated the activity.
pages.metrics.machinesDescription: Log-processor activity grouped by machine. Alert posts are the primary activity signal; heartbeats are shown separately.
pages.metrics.remediationMetricsNote: These are LAPI API counters. Dropped and processed traffic from a remediation component is reported through CrowdSec usage metrics and cannot be inferred from decision API calls.
pages.metrics.heartbeatLastSeenDescripti: Last heartbeat: {time}. Online means the machine reported within two minutes of this metrics scrape.
pages.metrics.heartbeatObservedDescripti: A heartbeat route was present in the cumulative Prometheus counters. This confirms that a heartbeat was observed since CrowdSec started, not that the machine is currently online.
pages.metrics.streamModeDescription: Stream mode uses /v1/decisions/stream. Empty/non-empty decision response counters describe live mode only, so they are not shown for this component.
pages.metrics.counterScope: Prometheus counters are cumulative since CrowdSec started; gauges show the current engine state.
pages.metrics.scenariosDescription: Scenario buckets show current activity and cumulative instantiation, overflow, poured, and expiry counters from the log processor.
pages.metrics.emptyScenarios: No scenario metrics were exposed by CrowdSec.
pages.metrics.parserSourcesDescription: Line-oriented parser activity by datasource. AppSec can appear here as a parser source; these counts are parser events, not AppSec HTTP request totals.
pages.metrics.parserSuccessTooltip: Parser success color: green is 80% or higher, amber is 50% to 80%, and gold is below 50%. Unparsed lines can be normal depending on your acquisition and parser setup.
pages.metrics.parserTimingDescription: Average parser processing time by source and type, derived from CrowdSec parsing histograms.
pages.metrics.parserNodesDescription: Per-parser-node processing inside CrowdSec. These rows show where parser events succeeded or stayed unparsed.
pages.metrics.whitelistsDescription: Whitelist node activity. Hits are lines evaluated by whitelist logic; whitelisted is the subset accepted by those rules.
pages.metrics.lapiLatencyDescription: Local API request counts by endpoint and method, with average duration when CrowdSec exposes the response-time histogram.
pages.metrics.appsecEnginesDescription: AppSec activity grouped by engine and source. Green shows allowed requests; amber shows blocked requests.
pages.metrics.emptyBouncers: No per-bouncer LAPI metrics were exposed by CrowdSec.

pages.metrics.appsecBlockRateTooltip: AppSec activity bar: green shows allowed requests for this engine/source, and amber shows blocked requests. The percentage is blocked requests divided by total AppSec requests in the current metrics counters.

pages.statistics.jobFailedHelp: The last statistics job failed. Pending observations are kept and processed again at the next scheduled run. Error: {error}
pages.statistics.comparisonPartial: A complete preceding period is not available for a reliable comparison.
pages.statistics.activityHistoryHelp: Alerts and decisions over time. Decisions are counted on their own creation date and include blocklist imports, so they can differ from the Remediations tile.
pages.statistics.detailsRetention: Applies these filters and the selected period as the quick filters on Alerts and Decisions, replacing the current ones. Details are kept for about {days} days; older details may no longer be available.
pages.statistics.disabledHelp: Collection is disabled. Previously collected statistics remain available until their retention expires. Enable collection in Settings to start building history.
pages.statistics.findingInBandScenario: {scenario} (AppSec) blocked {count} requests from {ips} IPs in-band; another scenario remediated {remediated} of these IPs.
pages.statistics.findingInBandScenarioNo: {scenario} (AppSec) blocked {count} requests from {ips} IPs in-band; no scenario remediated any of these IPs.
pages.statistics.findingInBandScenarioHe: AppSec rules block the matching request in-band and never issue a remediation themselves. Repeat offenders are remediated by a separate scenario that counts the rules an IP triggers, such as crowdsecurity/appsec-native or crowdsecurity/appsec-vpatch. Install one of them to keep such IPs out entirely, or ban them here.
pages.statistics.findingMachineSpike: {machine} received {current} alerts, up from {previous} in the preceding period.
pages.statistics.findingNetwork: {network} accounts for {percent}% of all alerts, from {ips} IPs. Consider blocking its address ranges.
pages.statistics.findingNetworkHelp: Blocking a range affects every address in it, including legitimate users of this provider. Prefer ranges with several attacking IPs.
pages.statistics.findingNewScenario: New attack type: {scenario} raised {count} alerts from {ips} IPs and was not seen in the preceding period.
pages.statistics.findingQuietMachine: {machine} raised no alerts in this period, after {count} in the preceding period. Check that its agent and log acquisition still run.
pages.statistics.findingReturnedAfterRem: {count} IPs attacked again on a later day after a remediation. Consider longer or stricter decisions.

A profile duration_expr can lengthen decisions for IPs that had decisions before, and a profile filter can ban repeat offenders instead of showing them a captcha. You can also ban these addresses for longer now.
pages.statistics.findingUnremediatedScen: {scenario} raised {count} alerts from {ips} IPs without a single remediation. Check that a profile remediates this scenario.

CrowdSec only issues a decision, such as a ban or captcha, when a profile matches the alert. Check that your profiles cover this scenario (for example Alert.Remediation == true with the Ip scope) and that it does not run in simulation mode.
pages.statistics.findingWideScanners: {count} of the top IPs attacked {machines} or more machines and are probing your infrastructure.
pages.statistics.loadError: Statistics are unavailable. If collection is enabled, wait for the next background job or retry.
pages.statistics.machineChangesHelp: Alerts per machine compared with the preceding period of the same length. Machines with unchanged counts are not listed.
pages.statistics.noFindings: No notable findings for this period.
pages.statistics.partial: This period has incomplete coverage. Counts reflect observed data; gaps in the chart do not mean zero attacks.
pages.statistics.rangeHint: Statistics use calendar days in {timeZone}. Dashboard totals use a rolling time window. Statistics also update separately, so counts may differ. Remediations in the tiles and rankings are counted on the date of their alert. Deleted alerts and expired decisions remain in the statistics.
pages.statistics.repeatAttackersHelp: Active on more than one day
pages.statistics.retentionHelp: Reducing retention permanently removes older statistics. Disabling collection preserves existing history until it expires. Exact IP statistics grow with the number of distinct attacker relationships.
pages.statistics.returnedAfterRemediatio: Attacked again on a later day
pages.statistics.deleteAllConfirm: This permanently deletes all collected statistics, including history that is no longer in the cache. If collection is enabled, it starts over with the alerts and decisions still in the cache.
pages.statistics.scenariosHelp: Remediations are alert decisions of any type, such as ban or captcha. Remediation coverage is the share of attacking IPs that received one for the scenario. AppSec rules block requests in-band, so for them the share remediated by any scenario is shown as well.
pages.statistics.settingsHelp: Collect compact daily summaries of cached alerts and decisions. Collection runs in the background and starts with available cached history.
